title: Hope

segments.voice: Yesterday: good courage, a first step taken because you aren't alone. Today, a father who wouldn't stop looking.

“I hope so,” about a job, a test result, a text that hasn't come back. In everyday talk, hope can sound like a coin tossed in a fountain. Here's an older picture. Jacob has lost his son Joseph, and both the Bible and the Qur'an tell that story. In the Qur'an's telling, Jacob, still grieving, sends his sons out to search for Joseph and his brother, and tells them not to despair of God's mercy. So what makes hope more than a wish?
screen: `I HOPE SO.` → `JACOB, STILL GRIEVING.` → `GO AND SEARCH.`

segments.voice: Paul answers with a ladder, in his letter to the Romans, and the bottom rung is trouble: “we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.” Trouble, then patience, then tested character, then hope. Hope grows through hard things, not around them. And it maketh not ashamed: it won't leave a person embarrassed for having held it, not because the odds are good, but because of a love already given. Hebrews gives it a picture: “an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.” An anchor works out of sight, under the water, while the surface tosses. Now the neighbor. Muslims read Surah Yusuf, where Jacob tells his sons that only those who reject God despair of his mercy. Christians and Muslims share this: hope that keeps searching in grief, rooted in God, not in luck. And one honest difference. Paul ties hope to the Holy Ghost poured into the heart, and to Christ. Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as God's Son, and the Qur'an roots Jacob's hope in God's mercy. Two scriptures, one grieving father, the same refusal to give up.
screen: `TROUBLE IS THE BOTTOM RUNG.` · `HOPE MAKETH NOT ASHAMED.` · `AN ANCHOR OUT OF SIGHT.` · `JACOB IN THE QUR'AN: DON'T DESPAIR.` · then, large: `HOPE HOLDS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person going through something hard. Write them one short line of hope: not a prediction of how it will turn out, just that you're holding on for them. Send it, or keep it, and if you pray, pray for them by name.
Hope. A steady expectation of good that grows through trouble and holds, like an anchor out of sight.
The line: hope holds, out of sight, like an anchor under the water. Day seventeen forty-two.

chat.says: nia asked how i stay hopeful about pop. she's not religious. what do i even tell her?
options: Hope isn't betting on odds. It's an anchor, holding to good not seen yet.
Tell her hope means knowing for sure it'll all turn out fine.
Say hope is just positive thinking; if she tries hard, it works.
chat.meaning: Paul says hope grows through trouble and doesn't rest on the odds; Hebrews calls it an anchor that holds out of sight. Hope is about what hasn't arrived.
